Women’s basketball stifled in 83-73 loss to Temple

By Ethan Tsai and Milo Rosenzweig
November 17, 2026
Rafael Torok | Photographer
Junior guard Jaeda Wilson dribbles during Tuesday’s game against Temple University.
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 5:36
Instaread

Women’s basketball (3-2) fell to Temple University (4-1) 83-73 Tuesday night at the Smith Center as the Revolutionaries celebrated Jonquel Jones — an MVP center for the New York Liberty of the WNBA who played with GW from 2013-2016 — with a jersey retirement ceremony. 

The Revolutionaries matched Temple’s intensity through the first two quarters, entering halftime down 34-33, but were stifled by aggressive defense and 53.5% shooting from beyond the arc by the Owls in the second half, an area where GW struggled throughout the game. Senior forward Sara Lewis emerged as Head Coach Ganiyat Adeduntan’s leading offensive performer for the second straight game, finishing the night with 21 points, including 90% shooting from the free throw line, before fouling out in the fourth quarter. 

The Revs probed the Owls in the paint throughout the first quarter, scoring 16 of 21 points on layups and jumpers. The Revs used sophomore forward N’na Konate to snatch offensive rebounds and finish missed baskets, while Lewis dominated in the paint, scoring seven points on layups and free throws from drawn fouls. 

The Revs pulled ahead by four before Temple retook the lead on two layups and a free throw from guard Taliya Logwood, who finished with 14 points after fouling out in the second half. Both teams kept responding quickly to each other, keeping the game within three points and closing the first quarter tied 19-19.

The Owls turned up their defensive intensity, squeezing the Revs’ shooting capabilities, but handing them ten points from the free throw line as a result. Lewis accounted for 8 of the Revs’ 14 points in the quarter, was fouled three times on drives to the basket and went 6-for-7 at the charity stripe. 

Despite committing 13 fouls in the first half, Temple took advantage of the Revs’ 1-for-10 shooting from three to end the half up 34-33.

The Revs came into the third quarter looking to get around Temple’s choking defensive strategy, focusing on quick passes to open teammates to punish the Owls for their tendency to apply pressure through double-teaming. An inside pass to Newell for a layup, her first of three in a 9-2 run, gave the Revs momentum and put them up 44-36 in the first four minutes of the quarter.

The Owls quickly closed the distance, however, answering with three layups and three shots from beyond the arc to come back and build a strong 52-46 lead. Layups from senior guard Amor Harris and graduate guard Anne Bair helped mitigate the damage, but the Revs’ inability to shut down Temple’s long-range game left them down 57-52 at the end of the third quarter. 

The fourth quarter turned into a footrace as both teams struggled to complete drives, facing stiff resistance as the defensive game reached its peak, but senior forward Kamari Sims, who finished the night with nine points, drove twice to the hoop in the early minutes of the quarter, finishing both a contested layup and a jump shot.

The Owls slowly widened the scoring gap over the final ten minutes, aided by six offensive rebounds compared to the Revs’ one, which let them finish at the basket and pull further ahead, leading 68-60 with five minutes remaining. Owl guards Mariah Cross and Kaylah Turner — who finished Tuesday with 16 and 21 points, respectively — traded three-pointers with junior guard Gabby Reynolds in the final minutes.

A last-minute corner three from Reynolds, with 16 seconds remaining, cut the Owl lead to 10, but Temple held on through the final buzzer to win 83-73.

Despite the loss, Adeduntan said she felt proud of how her team competed against Temple’s suffocating defense, as it provided the Revs opportunities to see where they need to improve.

“For us to have this kind of early test is always great, for us to measure up against a really great team to see where we are,” Adeduntan said. “Our philosophy always is in growing and getting better, and there’s going to be a lot to grow and get better at within this game.”

Before Tuesday’s matchup, Athletics honored Jones, who ranks fourth in scoring average in the program with 15.4 points per game and helped the Revs clinch two Atlantic 10 tournament titles and two A-10 regular-season titles. Jones, accompanied by her parents, watched her No. 35 banner appear beneath the Section 220 marker as the current Revs — sporting practice tees bearing Jones’ name, number, and an image of her on the front — joined the stadium in applause.

The ceremony also gave Temple Head Coach Diane Richardson, who recruited Jones and coached her during her tenure as an assistant coach at GW, a chance to reunite with the 2024 WNBA Finals MVP before the game.  

“I just didn’t imagine the type of impact that this place would have on me, and the amount of lasting memories and amazing people that I would get to meet on this journey,” Jones said, reflecting on her time in Foggy Bottom. “So, just a full circle moment tonight.”

Adeduntan also celebrated Jones, who she said spent Monday getting to know her players individually, calling her a “special human.” 

“That tells you the type of character that she is,” Adeduntan said. “On top of being a really great decorated player, the thing that stands out to me is, great players come here to GW, and I have a roster full of great players. And the hope is we continue to recruit great players who understand that you can become a champion here, and that’s what Jonquel has been able to do while she was here at GW, and then in her professional life.”

The Revs will face Howard University next on Nov. 20 at 7:00 p.m.

Ethan Tsai, Copy Chief
Ethan Tsai, a junior from Portland, Oregon, is majoring in international affairs and Chinese. Ethan is The Hatchet’s Copy Chief for its 123rd volume, sits on the Editorial Board and contributes as a staff writer for the Sports section. You can reach him @ethantsai06 on Instagram.
Milo Rosenzweig, Sports Editor
Milo Rosenzweig is a senior from Connecticut, majoring in journalism. Milo is The Hatchet’s Sports Editor for the paper’s 123rd volume, having previously dabbled in various sections, including news and video. He is reachable @miloprosenzweig on X.
